Active Cores are grouped in sets that correlate to a given frequency ratio multiplier. As the number of active cores goes up the frequency gets stepped down to avoid thermal throttling. The active core count that determines when the ratio step down occurs can be adjusted using the arrows or editing the input value in the lower or upper range. If the ratio of a group is changed to match the ratio of another group those groups will be joined together along with all groups inbetween.

To improve system performance, you can increase the ratio for each component. However, you may experience system instability during the overclocking process. System will be restored to a functional state on reboot.

To overclock your system, it is recommended to increment core ratio and voltage by small steps, apply the changes, then ensure system stability. You can do this cycle multiple times to get the best stable performance. To overclock other components (memory, cache, and others) or individual core behavior, switch to Advanced View.
